description: TRU First-year engineering students. A second group with the new task
summary: For our project, we covered the challenge of identifying earth locations that analog permanent moon base locations and Mars. In our specific research, we chose to look into the ways analogs are chosen on earth, and what is considered when comparing environmental factors, specifically, how these different environmental factors effect certain systems and how they would be tested, in order to find specific regions on Earth. We wrote a report on how we chose specific locations and the what they are best suited for.
details: No location on earth perfectly analogs Mars, and many of the best analogs can only cover every environmental factor so well. We considered this a case of quantity over quality, as while having an environment as similar as possible in all categories seems important, not every factor is always as important, and sometimes finding somewhere that matches some environmental factors very well, is better than one that matches all but only a bit. Specific systems used by NASA are affected by different parts of the environment, so by only focusing on the relevant factors, it’s possible to find a much better analog for testing a specific system. We chose to test this by finding possible analogs for four different systems, those being navigation sensors, rover materials, landing systems, and base construction.
